candidate.title: fCAB-Seq
candidate.scope: EtONH2 protection-based fCAB-Seq at the assigned Illumina poster row: DNA containing 5fC is represented in paired unprotected-control and O-ethylhydroxylamine-protected branches, each separately subjected to the drawn bisulfite treatment/PCR amplification block. The diagram inventory is C/5mC/5hmC/5fC/5caC input, Control versus EtONH2 arrows, Blocked 5fC, T C C T T versus T C C C T products, and a generic final DNA icon. The title, row caption and matching catalogue heading identify fCAB-Seq alone. Neighboring partial oxBS-Seq, RedBS-Seq/caMAB-seq and MAB-seq rows, and the separate right-edge Biotin/chemical legend, are context without a route into this row. Neither those workflows nor fC-Seal, ChIP-fCAB-Seq, fC-CET or RNA adaptations are target alternatives of this card. This is the shared schematic architecture, not a complete adapter-bearing library recipe or a claim of identical complete implementations across cited applications.

operations.label: O-ethylhydroxylamine (EtONH2)
operations.description: Treat the lower DNA arm with the named reagent so that the original 5fC residue becomes the depicted Blocked residue. Other depicted cytosine classes retain their identities at this boundary.
operations.mechanism: O-ethylhydroxylamine-based protection of 5fC against bisulfite-mediated deamination; no adduct formula is inferred from the icon.
operations.information_effect: Preserves original 5fC sites as bisulfite-resistant sites on DNA, enabling a subsequent C-versus-T comparison with the control.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process the unprotected control DNA through the depicted combined block. The resulting amplified DNA has T at originally C, 5fC and 5caC positions, and C at originally 5mC and 5hmC positions: T C C T T.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite conversion followed by PCR encodes the illustrated base-conversion pattern in DNA sequence. The primary paper specifies that unprotected 5fC can be converted to uracil during bisulfite sequencing.
operations.information_effect: Establishes the conventional bisulfite C signal from 5mC plus 5hmC; the original 5fC signal is lost into the T class in this arm.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process the EtONH2-protected DNA through its separate instance of the depicted combined block. The resulting amplified DNA has T at originally C and 5caC positions and C at originally 5mC, 5hmC and protected 5fC positions: T C C C T.
operations.mechanism: Protection prevents 5fC bisulfite-mediated deamination, and PCR yields C at that site while the remaining positions follow the depicted conversion pattern.
operations.information_effect: The sequenced carrier is amplified DNA. Compared with the control at corresponding genomic positions, additional C retention reports original 5fC at base resolution. This is a paired differential readout, not a unique 5fC assignment from every C in a treated read. The schematic idealizes conversion and does not establish perfect protection or conversion efficiency. Sequencing and signal comparison are paper-supported interpretation of the output, not separately drawn operations.
